issue_context.title: sql: implement a cache of table descriptors with type metadata
issue_context.body: Currently, when an immutable table descriptor with user defined types is resolved it is copied before type metadata is installed in it. We should have a caching layer above the lease manager but below the `desc.Collection` that holds on to `ImmutableTableDescriptor`s with hydrated type metadata. This layer will store multiple versions of each `ImmutableTableDescriptor` as there could be tables with different versions of the contained types in use by the node.
comments:
I was trying to iron out some details here, and the read paths seem pretty straightforward. What I'm not sure about is how evictions will work. If we maintain a reference count and evict when it hits 0, this cache is basically part of the `desc.Collection` -- if we use and hydrate a table, then end the txn, then use the same table and types again in another transaction we'll have to allocate again. So it seems like the elements in the cache need to be longer lived than the references created by the `desc.Collection`. The only other choice is to follow lease drops on tables and types. If we drop a lease on a table or type, all entries in this cache needs to be dropped. However, this makes it seem like it won't be possible to have this cache be a layer on top of the lease manager.

Do you have thoughts on this @ajwerner? I know you mentioned that you were thinking about giving this a try.
Discussed offline -- conclusion is to start out with just using an LRU cache or an equivalent and maintain a maximum number of descriptors in the structure.

review_comments: Add a comment about the fact that we might get rejected from the cache if we have an uncommitted descriptor, or if any of the types referenced are uncommitted too

2) Augment the cache built here to have a cache for the underlying `*types.T` values and utilize those when hydrating descriptors to avoid just a few allocs.
